name: Yelena Belova

summary: Yelena Belova was born in Russia and raised in Moscow's Red Room Academy, the program that turns girls into Black Widow agents. Determined to make her parents proud, she set out to become the finest Widow there had ever been, and her test results were said to beat those of Natasha Romanoff, the Widow who had defected to the West. Unlike most cadets she was drilled almost entirely on the physical side, a gap in her psychological training that would cost her later. She was ruthless early: at twelve she killed her coach at the gymnastics federation. In the academy she rose to the rank of captain and grew close to her instructor, Colonel Starkovsky, and to the Red Room physician Lika Medvedev.

Her real test came when Starkovsky was found murdered in a fetish club and General Tischenko put her on the case. The club's manager, Nikki, seemed to know far too much about the Widow program, and Yelena learned that her mentor had been paying for time with a woman called Petra who dressed in a copy of Yelena's own uniform. When a police detective turned up dead in Petra's rooms, Yelena tracked her down: Petra had read leaked Red Room files and wanted to be the only Black Widow. Yelena was shot in the fight but killed her rival, then buried her grief. What she never learned was that Nikki was a Red Room captain and that the whole affair had been staged to harden her into a true Widow.

Now carrying the Black Widow codename, Yelena was attached to Colonel Yuri Stalyenko. In her first appearance she acts as a go-between with an American agent named Bixby, handing over a device supplied by Maximus the Mad that was meant to give the human nations an edge against the Inhumans' city of Attilan. Above all she was fixated on Natasha, whom she both idolised and resented, and she was eager for the chance to prove herself the better spy.

comics.title: The itsy-bitsy spider
comics.summary: At her own insistence Yelena is sent to shadow Natasha, who has been dispatched to the small nation of Rhapastan to deal with a bioweapon called the Deathless Frenzy. After spying on her for days, Yelena fights beside her rival against Rhapastani troops, then follows her to Zurich. Fooled into thinking S.H.I.E.L.D. agents have shot Natasha dead, she takes over the mission against Colonel Khan, fails and is captured, and has to be saved by Natasha, who tells her that passion has no place in spy work.

comics.title: Wearing her rival's face
comics.summary: To show Yelena what spying really means, Natasha has Nick Fury's agents abduct her and surgically swap their faces. Waking in Natasha's apartment, Yelena is pointed at a target named Yelena Belova, really Natasha in disguise, while a reluctant Daredevil helps her hold on to who she is. When she secretly watches Stalyenko describe her as a disposable tool, she turns on her master and knocks him out, then confronts Natasha, calls the scheme a violation of her identity and demands her own face back.

comics.title: Havana
comics.summary: Yelena steps away from espionage for a while and builds a lingerie business out of Havana, using it to protect sex workers and get HIV medication to people who need it. With the old rivalry behind her, she gives a hunted Natasha a safe place to hide and asks for help moving medical supplies out of Miami. When the operatives Kestrel and Martin Ferris capture Natasha and try to drug her secrets out of her, Yelena teams up with Daredevil to get her out.

comics.title: A weapon built for revenge
comics.summary: Back in the field as a freelance S.H.I.E.L.D. operative, Yelena is part of a rogue unit using enslaved locals to mine vibranium in the Savage Land, and she orders her troops to open fire on the New Avengers. Sauron leaves her horribly burned, and a Hydra agent offers to rebuild her: A.I.M. scientists turn her into a living Super-Adaptoid aimed at the Avengers. She storms their tower around the time of Luke Cage and Jessica Jones' wedding, soaking up the team's powers, including the Sentry's and the instability of his dark side, the Void, until her handlers kill her with a remote failsafe.

comics.title: A borrowed name on the Thunderbolts
comics.summary: After the Skrull invasion Norman Osborn appears to find Yelena looting an abandoned S.H.I.E.L.D. base and makes her field leader of his Thunderbolts. The Widow on the team is really Natasha in disguise, planted by Nick Fury. Osborn knew all along and used her to reach Fury and Songbird; he fails to hurt any of them but does get hold of the real Yelena's body, which he keeps at Avengers Tower.

comics.title: Minister of State
comics.summary: Recovered by A.I.M., Yelena joins its High Council as Minister of State of the group's new island nation in Barbuda and pushes for an army, backed by Taskmaster, who is secretly a double agent. Using her Adaptoid powers she helps steal the Iron Patriot armour from a weapons expo, killing Senator Rebel Ralston, and later nearly kills Natasha before Hawkeye saves her. She captures a S.H.I.E.L.D. team sent to rescue Mockingbird, but in a fight Mockingbird slips her own holographic disguise onto Yelena, and an A.I.M. soldier guns Yelena down thinking she is the escaped Avenger.

comics.title: The Red Ledger clones
comics.summary: A revived Red Room has been growing clones of its best agents, Yelena among them. Natasha, now a clone herself, secretly wakes three blank Yelena bodies, apparently after killing the original, uses two in her schemes and destroys the program, sparing only the third; to make amends she has the psychic Epsilon Red give it the real Yelena's memories, though not her Adaptoid powers. Later, hired by the billionaire Justin Cask to break a prisoner out of an Antarctic facility in a white version of her old suit, Yelena realises she is only there as target practice, frees the imprisoned Red Guardian instead, and empties Cask's bank accounts into charities.

comics.title: Ally to Natasha, partner to Alexei
comics.summary: When Natasha's enemies brainwash her into a quiet life in San Francisco as an architect with a husband and son, Yelena slips into her household as a babysitter called Helen and helps her break free once her memories return. Taking the name White Widow, she becomes Natasha's ally and helps train young women to look after themselves. She also teams with Alexei Shostakov to recover hard drives exposing old Soviet corruption, flying on a knock-off set of Falcon wings, only for him to leave her to the Winter Guard and run off with the last drive.

comics.title: Idylhaven and the Thunderbolts
comics.summary: After Captain America interrupts one of her contracts and urges her to use her skills for good, Yelena moves to the small town of Idylhaven with her dog, Bint Clarton, and starts a wall listing everything she has an opinion on. The town turns out to be a training ground for Armament Industries' assassins and robots, and once they wreck a neighbour's shop, take over her coffee place and attack her at home, she brings the company down with help from her neighbour Griffin LaChance, killing its hidden owner Renata Best. Having found she likes being on a team, she joins Bucky Barnes' Thunderbolts to seize the Red Skull's fortune and hunt him down in Latveria.

comics.title: Blood Hunters
comics.summary: When vampires overrun the world, Yelena is turned and goes hunting in Brooklyn until Elsa Bloodstone pins her down and Dagger burns the curse out of her with her light, briefly taking it on herself. Yelena repays the debt by stopping Elsa from killing the infected Dagger, and with Hallows' Eve the four form the Blood Hunters. After the event, with vampires now able to walk in daylight, Yelena leads the raid to rescue Dagger from the super-powered Bloodcoven, survives being possessed by Smoke Eater, and watches Cloak trap the vampires in the Darkforce before the team agrees to part until it is needed again.

screen.title: Black Widow
screen.actor: Florence Pugh (Violet McGraw as young Yelena)
screen.summary: Yelena is introduced as a Red Room assassin who spent part of her childhood believing a Soviet cover family in Ohio was real, before being returned to the program. In 2016 a dose of the Red Dust antidote breaks Dreykov's chemical hold on her, and she reunites with Natasha, helps spring Alexei from prison, frees the brainwashed Widows with a Red Dust bomb and destroys Dreykov's escape craft, killing him. In the post-credits scene, set in 2024, she mourns at Natasha's grave and Valentina Allegra de Fontaine gives her a new target, Clint Barton, blaming him for her sister's death.

screen.title: Hawkeye
screen.summary: Yelena appears in the last three episodes, first as a masked attacker who ambushes Clint and Kate Bishop on a rooftop until Clint pulls off her mask, while a flashback shows her vanishing in the Blip in 2018 and returning five years later. She discovers that Kate's mother Eleanor hired her and sends Kate footage of Eleanor meeting the Kingpin. On Christmas Eve she finally corners Clint on the ice at Rockefeller Center, but when he tells her how Natasha sacrificed herself and whistles their private signal, she lets him go.

screen.title: Thunderbolts*
screen.actor: Florence Pugh (Violet McGraw as young Yelena)
screen.summary: Depressed and drinking, Yelena is still cleaning up after Valentina when she is sent to a sealed vault to be disposed of alongside other expendable operatives; she escapes with John Walker, Ghost and the mysterious Bob, and the group ends up named after her childhood soccer team, the Thunderbolts. When Bob's dark side, the Void, engulfs New York, she walks into the darkness to reach him and helps him face his pain, and when Valentina spins the group as the New Avengers she quietly tells her that the team now owns her. In the post-credits scene, set fourteen months later, she grumbles about Sam Wilson's trademark fight over the Avengers name as the team spots an extra-dimensional ship bearing a "4".

screen.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day
screen.summary: Now publicly known as Black Widow and a New Avenger, Yelena receives Spider-Man in the sauna she uses as an office, tells him the culprit behind attacks on Damage Control has been digging for something called "V-Max", and declines to get involved in what she calls a small-scale problem while teasing him about working alone. Later, on a video call, she tells him that Jean Grey's sister Sara was taken by Damage Control, and is pleased to see he has friends when MJ and Ned crowd into the frame.

unverified: Avengers: Doomsday and Avengers: Secret Wars appear in the MCU Wiki infobox for Yelena but are marked unreleased, so they are left out. No plot details were researched.

Avengers: Endgame Encore re-release (25 September 2026): the MCU Wiki's Encore plot summary and Encore-exclusive cast list do not include Yelena. The only related item on the Endgame page is "Yelena Belova's Vest", the prop Natasha wears, so no entry was added.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day: the MCU Wiki says the film "will be" re-released with additional footage; that version is not treated as released by 2026-10-25 and was not checked. The cameo flag is a judgement call: Pugh is billed among the main cast and the wiki does not tag the role as a cameo, but she appears in only two short scenes. The MCU Wiki character page also describes Yelena meeting Jean DeWolff in her sauna office, but the film's plot summary only has DeWolff mention it, so it is not described as an on-screen scene.

Animated and voice-only work is left out: the Marvel Fandom wiki notes that Florence Pugh voiced a Yelena variant in the animated Marvel Zombies series. The Thunderbolts* Dossier (in-universe files listed by the MCU Wiki) is not a film or series and is also left out.
No non-MCU live-action version of Yelena was found; the Marvel Fandom disambiguation page lists no film or TV counterpart other than Earth-199999.
Date conflict: the Marvel Fandom Earth-199999 page places the Ohio family's escape in 1996, while the MCU Wiki and the Black Widow film plot say 1995. The screen summary avoids the year.

Venom Vol 7 #1 (cover date December 2026, released 14 October 2026) lists Yelena as appearing, and the Earth-616 page notes that she begins dating Eddie Brock and the Venom symbiote in that series, but that note is sourced to an outside news article and the issue page has no synopsis. It is left out of the eras.

The original Yelena's death in Tales of Suspense #103-104 is described on the Earth-616 page as something Natasha 'allegedly' did; the confirmation the wiki cites is a writer's social media post, not the comic. The era says 'apparently'.

Several issue pages used here (Black Widow: Pale Little Spider #1 and #3, Black Widow 2 #1 and #6, Tales of Suspense #103-104, Widowmakers #1, Secret Avengers #15, White Widow #1 and #4, Thunderbolts Vol 6 #2 and #4, Blood Hunters, Winter Guard) have no plot synopsis. Details from them, including the gymnastics coach killing cited to Thunderbolts Vol 6 #2, rest on the Earth-616 character page plus solicitations.

The Earth-616 page tells the Havana era (Black Widow 2, cover dates 2005-2006) before the Savage Land story (New Avengers #6, June 2005); the eras follow the page's order. A hidden comment in the page's source mentions a stint with the black-ops team Vanguard (Marvel Comics Presents Vol 2 #12); it is not shown on the live page and was left out.
Creators: the Marvel Fandom wiki lists all four of Devin Grayson, J.G. Jones, Paul Jenkins and Jae Lee, and notes that Grayson and Jones are her actual creators. All four are kept to match the wiki.
